## Verdict

missing

## Bearer

Race — core-domain/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/domain/race/Race.kt

## Trigger

RecordedRaceSyncService.sync, right after `transport.send(payload)`
succeeds for a race — observed

## Today

`Race` carries `id`/`name`/`date`/`origin`/`isReference`/`completion`/
`segments`/`retainedFactors`/`rejectedCalibrations`/
`currentSegmentIndex`/`currentSegmentOpenedAt` — nothing distinguishing
a race the watch has already sent to the phone from one it has not.
`RaceRecordingRepositoryImpl.observeRecorded()` returns every race with
no current segment, sent or not, and `RecordedRaceSyncService.sync`
iterates that same list on every call: it sends, then saves on the
phone via `raceRepository.saveRecordedRace`, then erases via
`raceRecordingRepository.eraseRecorded(race.id)`. If the watch process
is interrupted after `transport.send` succeeds but before
`eraseRecorded` runs — e.g. mid-loop over several races, after an
earlier race in the same call already finished — the next `sync()`
call finds that race still present with nothing marking it as already
sent, and sends it again.

## Expected

`Race` carries an explicit state telling a sent-but-unacknowledged race
apart from one never sent — e.g. a `sent: Boolean` or `sentAt: Instant?`
field, false/null until the watch confirms delivery.
`RaceRecordingRepository` gains a way to set that state on a given
race id — no such method exists today, and `RecordedRaceSyncService`
needs one to call right after `transport.send` succeeds, before
`saveRecordedRace`/`eraseRecorded` run. `observeRecorded` keeps
returning the race regardless of that state — sent or not, it stays in
the watch's own history until `eraseRecorded` runs on the phone's
acknowledgement — but `RecordedRaceSyncService.sync` reads the state
before resending: a race already marked sent is not sent a second
time, only (re)saved/erased if that step had not completed yet.
